dial.summary: DXY rebounded to 100.27 on September 21's NY open, reversing Saturday's weekend-FX dip to 99.09 and restoring the dollar headwind alongside elevated real yields at 2.66%, leaving two structural obstacles against three supportive forces (M2 expanding at $103.5T, Fed balance sheet flat at $6.75T, near-zero BTC funding at 0.008%); TOTAL crypto fully recovered from September 20's $2.75T pullback to retest $2.87T with BTC.D firming to 56.92% and stablecoin dominance easing to 10.66%, confirming continued spot-driven BTC accumulation ahead of the data-dense September 30 triple-release (PCE, GDP, ADP) and October 2 NFP.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $103,511B (~$103.5T) as of September 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week lag; July is the last fully reported month); US M2 alone reached $23.2T in July 2026; 4-week trend up confirmed (sustained expansion from ~$103.0T in late August to $103.5T in mid-September); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%) will modestly affect yen-denominated G4 components going forward but has no near-term impact on the reported aggregate.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM not released until October 1; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); S&P Global Flash PMI September 23 is the next advance read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY rebounded to 100.27 on September 21, 2026 (NY open, up 0.05% from Friday's 100.21 official close), reversing the weekend FX dip to 99.09 (Saturday illiquid FX, non-representative) as the BOJ-driven yen-surge effect faded and week-opening USD demand returned; 4-week trend up: ~99.0 (Aug 21) → 100.27 (Sep 21) = +1.27%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY has returned above the 100 threshold, shifting from the prior session's neutral reading which was based on an unrepresentative weekend FX quote; DXY above 100 now joins real yields at 2.66% as the second structural macro headwind; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) closed at 2.66% on September 18, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.15; FRED H.15 released September 21 covers through September 19 but the confirmed latest is September 18 at 2.66%; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 19) → 2.66% (Sep 18) = +21bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); real yields remain the primary macro drag on duration-sensitive and risk assets; DXY returning to 100.27 headwind status means two macro headwinds are now active simultaneously; sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 19–21, 2026: 10Y ~5.01%, 2Y ~4.75% (per US Treasury market data); spread = +0.26% (+26bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 18, pre-FOMC) → +26bps (Sep 21) = −12bps, driven by front-end repricing as 2Y anchors to the fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); curve remains positively sloped but compressed 12bps over 4 weeks as real yield pressure keeps the 10Y elevated while the 2Y is anchored to the policy rate; the October 27–28 FOMC will be the next key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 17 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 24, 2026; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B, marginal expansion within the flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilisation plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity, not new asset purchases); total assets up $138B year-on-year (from $6,609B).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.008% per 8h (range 0.0073%–0.0085% per 8h per MacroMicro/TheBlock as of September 18–21, 2026); near-zero funding during both the September 20 $2.75T TOTAL pullback and the September 21 full recovery to $2.87T confirms both legs were spot-driven, not leveraged speculation; 30-day trend flat (funding has remained sub-0.01% throughout September as accumulation was orderly); status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; near-zero is the ideal accumulation signal).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (September 21, 2026; CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap); total crypto market cap $2.87T (TOTAL fully recovered from September 20's $2.75T pullback to retest the September 19 high of $2.87T); stablecoin dominance 10.66% ($307B / $2.87T); 30-day trend down: from ~11%+ (August 20) → 10.66% (Sep 21) = clear declining trend as capital deployed into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply as dominance is declining); BTC dominance at 56.92% ($1.64T of $2.87T total); USDT $183.4B (60.57%), USDC $74.2B (24.1%); sustained sub-11% dominance alongside BTC.D firmly above 55% is the primary BTC Accumulation signal this cycle.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance September activity read capturing the full post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) tightening cluster; DXY has rebounded to 100.27 on Monday as the BOJ-driven weekend dip corrected, restoring the dollar headwind entering the first advance read; leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services; a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially shift November FOMC rate-path narrative; consensus expects modest softening from prior reads.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 20, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 20, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks under fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; prior weeks approximately 206K; labor resilience is key to the FOMC's case for sustained restrictive policy heading into October 27–28.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~5.01%, real yields 2.66%) and DXY back at 100.27 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.
